newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Nato seeks closer ties with Mediterranean states.
newsitem.headline: Nato seeks closer ties with Mediterranean states.

text.p: NATO ministers agreed on Thursday to push for closer ties with Mediterranean basin countries to ensure that Europe's southern flank was not overlooked in the rush to expand the alliance eastwards.

Foreign ministers, meeting here to prepare to bring new members from eastern Europe into the 16-nation group, said that contacts with the Mediterranean rim should be put on a formal footing through the setting up of a special committee.
"We...recommend to our heads of state and government to formally establish...a new committee to have overall responsibility for the Mediterranean dialogue," the ministers said in a communique.
Ministers said that they were pleased with the development of dialogue between NATO and a number of countries in the Mediterranean region.
But the aim of the new committee would be to "enhance this dialogue and improve its overall political visibility".

Italian foreign minister Lamberto Dini said that the eventual aim could be to establish a "Partnership for Peace" for the Mediterranean countries along the lines of the association formed with former Soviet bloc and other eastern European countries after the collapse of communism there.
"A Partnership for Peace should be the objective but it needs time to be prepared. It is an ongoing process which we want to see accelerated," he told journalists.

The two-day meeting is to lay the groundwork for a summit in Madrid in July at which NATO will decide which candidate countries from the former Soviet bloc will be admitted to membership in the first wave.
